name: nsenter
description: Enters the namespaces of an existing process — how you attach to containers and inspect other processes' worlds.

flags.description: Target process whose namespaces to enter.
Enter mount / UTS / IPC / network / PID namespace (default: all).

examples.explanation: Runs ip a inside PID 2140's network namespace — shows a container's interfaces from the host.
A shell inside a process's mount and PID namespaces — manual container debugging without docker exec.

about: nsenter is the inverse of unshare: instead of creating new namespaces, it joins existing ones via /proc/PID/ns/*. It requires root (or matching user-namespace ownership). It works even where docker exec cannot — on crashed containers or non-container namespaces.
mistakes: Forgetting -t and wondering what it entered.
Expecting it to work without root for other users' processes.
